messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: control-plane.p95/p99 latency SLO breached for inference-config-fetch (service: cfg-service). Current window: p95=420ms p99=2.8s, streaming stalls observed. Auto-page oncall.

maya (oncall): seen. paging Ian. I'm going to grab initial blast radius and customer impact.

ian (sre): on it. I can see a spike in cfg-service DB latency and a flurry of auth token DB locks. Likely contention on token lookup table. p99 for auth-db queries ~2.5s. Streaming stall traces show many requests stuck waiting for config fetch.

maya (oncall): thanks. alex, any recent deploys to cfg-service or feature-flag changes?

alex (platform): we rolled a small change to the feature-flag sync yesterday at 21:10 UTC — it touched the token cache invalidation path. Jira RF-4212. No infra changes.

jen (prod-eng): that release was a hotfix for flag evaluation ordering. Rolling forward seemed clean in staging.

ian (sre): attaching quick snapshot logs (excerpt):

```
2026-02-14T21:33:11Z cfg-service ERROR fetch_config user=acct_123 db_query_time=2567ms rows=1
2026-02-14T21:33:12Z auth-db WARN deadlock detected pid=3421 waiting=auth_tokens_lookup
2026-02-14T21:33:13Z cfg-service WARN streaming stall id=req_9a7a t_wait=1800ms waiting_for=config_fetch
```

ian (sre): also ran `pg_stat_activity` — many backends in idle in transaction around token lookup. Suspect missing index or a bad transaction scope introduced in the hotfix.

maya (oncall): impact? which customers and how many requests?

ian (sre): rough numbers from metrics: ~12 customers had streaming stalls >= 1s over the last 12m, total affected requests ~3.6k. Error rates for streaming responses increased by 4.3%. No data exfiltration; reads only.

maya (oncall): escalation policy? severity 2? paging SRE and prod-eng already.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev 2 by maya (oncall). Notifying leadership channel.

ian (sre): short-term mitigations I propose:
- flip cfg-service to use cached config TTL=300s (fail-open) to avoid live DB reads for every request
- temporarily increase DB connection pool for cfg-service by +20
- revert the hotfix for feature-flag invalidation (RF-4212) if rollback safe
- remove a transactional wrapper around token lookup introduced in change (if safe)

alex (platform): I can set the cache TTL and bump pool size via infra config. Issuing change now.

alex (platform): executed: `kubectl set env deploy/cfg-service CFG_CACHE_TTL=300` and `helm upgrade --set cfgService.dbPoolSize=60 cfg-service ...` — new config rolling.

deploy-bot: deploy cfg-service/2026-02-14_21:45 started by alex.

jen (prod-eng): I'll prepare a safe rollback patch for RF-4212. Can we cut the rollback after cache TTL stabilizes?

ian (sre): yes. try to rollback only the token-invalidation part; if rollback risky, toggle the gating flag to disable the new path.

maya (oncall): monitoring: enable short alert rule: p99 cfg-service > 1.5s -> notify #incidents.

ian (sre): after cache TTL change, early signals: p95 dropped to 120ms, p99 to 400ms within ~90s. Streaming stall traces are clearing. DB active locks dropped by ~85%.

maya (oncall): awesome. alex, keep the cache in place until root cause confirmed and fixed. jen, coordinate rollback window and postmortem.

jen (prod-eng): started rollback branch and test. If all green, I'll cut rollback in 15m.

ian (sre): I'll run index check and a quick explain on token lookup:
```
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM auth_tokens WHERE user_id=$1 AND token_hash=$2;
-- shows seq scan 2.3s
```
We may need to add a composite index on (user_id, token_hash). I'll prepare the change but won't apply without rollout plan.

alex (platform): DB team — heads up, we might add index. Any concerns about index build locks on production?

ian (sre): will do concurrent index if Postgres supports it for our version. Plan: concurrent index build, low IO window.

deploy-bot: deploy cfg-service/2026-02-14_21:47 succeeded.

ian (sre): p99 remains under 500ms. Rolling mitigations are working. We still should rollback the faulty code path to remove coupling between config fetch and token store transactions.

jen (prod-eng): launching rollback now (RF-4212 revert). Patch applied, testing in canary.

jen (prod-eng): canary looks good. Rolling revert to 50% then 100%.

deploy-bot: revert RF-4212 deployed to cfg-service — rollout complete.

ian (sre): post-revert checks: db locks returned to baseline, p99 ~ 180ms, streaming stalls resolved. Good.

maya (oncall): customer impact summary for postmortem draft: ~3.6k requests affected, 12 customers saw degraded streaming for ~4-12 minutes each, SLO breach window ~12 minutes. No requests failed permanently — retries recovered most streams.

alex (platform): I'll keep CFG_CACHE_TTL=300 for the next 24h and disable aggressive token invalidation.

jen (prod-eng): opened postmortem doc: https://redwood/docs/postmortems/RF-4212-configfetch-latency (draft). Assigning root-cause owner: jen, remediation owner: ian.

maya (oncall): handing off to next oncall (maya -> night-oncall Sam) in 30m. Sam, please watch p99 and the cache TTL.

sam (night-oncall): ack — I'll take over at shift handoff.

ian (sre): short-term action items (for postmortem):
- add concurrent index on auth_tokens (owner: ian)
- add automated perf test for config fetch under token churn (owner: jen)
- improve deploy-time testing for feature-flag code paths (owner: alex)
- add runbook step: on p99 spikes, toggle CFG_CACHE_TTL to 300s and revert RF-4212 (owner: maya)

maya (oncall): closing incident thread once handoff complete and metrics stable for 1h. Great work all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident severity set to RESOLVED by maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): last check 30m later: p95=95ms p99=210ms, no new stalls. Closing.
